difficulty.basis: Recognize the set inclusion Q ⊂ R and reject narrower sets that do not contain every rational number.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Choosing integer, whole or natural because familiar examples of rational numbers happen to lie in those narrower sets.
grade9v3:analysis.stable_crux_move: Use the universal set-inclusion claim: every rational number is a real number, while not every rational number is integer, whole or natural.

reasoning: A rational number is, by definition, a number that can be written as p/q with integers p and q and q non-zero; every such number is a real number.
The narrower sets do not contain every rational number: for example, 1/2 is rational but is not an integer, whole number or natural number.
Therefore the only option true for every rational number is (C) a real number.

reasoning_route.action: Read the word every as a set-inclusion claim about all rational numbers.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A universal multiple-choice statement is true only if every member of the source set belongs to the chosen target set.
reasoning_route.output: Test which option names a set containing all rational numbers.

reasoning_route.action: Use Q ⊂ R and contrast it with the narrower natural, whole and integer sets.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Every rational number is real, but rationals such as 1/2 are outside the natural, whole and integer sets.
reasoning_route.output: Only the real-number option survives the universal claim.

reasoning_route.action: Check the surviving statement against a non-integer rational example.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A counterexample rejects a universal statement; 1/2 rejects A, B and D but not C.
reasoning_route.output: Option (C) is consistent with every rational number.

answer.check: Use 1/2: it is rational and real, but not natural, whole or integer.

scaffolds.text: Focus on the word every. You need a set that contains all rational numbers, not just some familiar examples.
scaffolds.prompt: Which option claims the broadest guaranteed membership?

scaffolds.text: Use 1/2 as a boundary example: it is rational but not an integer, whole number or natural number.
scaffolds.prompt: Which three options fail on this one rational number?

scaffolds.text: Now use the inclusion Q ⊂ R: every rational number belongs to the real numbers.
scaffolds.prompt: Which remaining option states that inclusion?
